description: Join my team! I've researched 3D mapping for GPS-denied Martian caves using LiDAR, infrared, and math for future astronaut missions. Winner of Anahuac Veracruz’s SerAnahuac Research & Science Award, with experience at Brazil's FETEPS science fair and hydroponics projects in Querétaro. Let's build this Mars exploration tech together!
summary: For the Interplanetary Survival Guide: Martian Map challenge, we developed PAPOI, an offline-first, interactive navigation and safety guide ("PAPOI") tailored for human astronauts exploring Jezero Crater.   What we developed: A single-file HTML/JavaScript application that integrates official multi-mission NASA and USGS datasets to map Perseverance’s historic traverse from POI 1 to POI 9. It adapts the rover's route for human-scale foot travel supported by a gear-carrying companion rover, featuring real-time safety traffic lights, slope warnings, oxygen limit calculations, and a dynamic 27-item equipment checklist.   How it addresses the challenge: It bridges the gap between complex robotic orbital data and human-scale mission execution, ensuring astronauts can safely navigate hazardous terrain, manage cargo, and execute contingency protocols without internet access.   Why it is important: As humanity prepares for crewed missions to Mars, transforming raw scientific data into practical, intuitive, real-time survival tools is critical to safeguarding astronaut lives and maximizing scientific discovery.
details: Our route and traverse plan adapts Perseverance’s actual path for human explorers accompanied by a support rover carrying heavy gear, with all necessary equipment and supplies seamlessly tracked and managed through our dynamic cargo checklist.
